answer: Sybil attackers fear one thing: an audit they cannot schedule. First, each epoch 2% of identities face a deep inspection proving unique operator work. Second, failures are banned instantly and locked rewards burn. Third, suspicion raises the draw rate to 20% nearby, so fraud clusters are exposed like sunbathers on a terrace, every blemish visible. Fourth, an attacker fielding 5,000 fakes loses 100 per epoch while feeding each $0.30 daily compute, $1,500 a day, plus $50 per replacement. A sybil farm is a cipher the network keeps decoding, and the key changes every tide.
